descriptors.claim: On their respective committed EdgeCases inputs, real javac scores every emitted method by one source-only rule. The scorer compiles the complete recovered source set first. If a parse failure blocks attribution, it isolates the implicated balanced method, field-initializer, or type region under a 64-round ceiling and reruns javac. Methods in isolated method or type regions are unclean. Peer methods count only after javac reaches attribution. A leg publishes a lead only when both sides are certified.
descriptors.comparison_basis: no comparison: at least one declared leg has a side the compiler never type-checked
descriptors.external_oracle: real javac (JDK), per-method recompile error-free against a STUBBED (empty) classpath so a wrong recovered signature cannot resolve against the original classes; one source-only scorer applies the same complete-compile, bounded region-isolation, and final diagnostic rule to every tool
descriptors.measured: Android DEX: `disrobe` 56 / 163 (34.4%) vs JADX not certified (295 methods emitted; the producer exited nonzero); JVM classfile: `disrobe` 181 / 181 (100.0%) vs CFR 152 / 166 (91.6%)

pairs.comparison_basis: none: a side of this leg was never type-checked

descriptors.claim: across the 316 committed mixed-boolean-arithmetic cases, every answer disrobe returns agrees with the held-out original, and a case whose simplification exceeds a 2 second per-entry budget is named as a refusal rather than counted either way. A reference run answered 247 cases, refused 69, and an external bitvector solver proved 236 of the answers equal to the original while refuting none.
descriptors.external_oracle: the originals are held out of the input the pass receives. 100 of the 316 cases were produced by MBA-Obfuscator (ICICS 2021, MIT, pinned at commit 8574ef8) run over integer kernels this repository chose, so their obfuscated form is third-party and the original is the pre-transform kernel. The other 216 come from a forward rewriter under evidence/generators/mba that links no disrobe crate at all, which the workspace health check proves over the resolved dependency graph. Grading has two legs: a behavioural differential against check vectors the generator computed with its own evaluator, so a wrong answer cannot agree with a value the recovery path produced, and z3 or bitwuzla proving the recovered expression equal to the held-out original over every input, which is exact rather than sampled.
descriptors.measured: 316 corpus entries with a held-out original

descriptors.claim: disrobe reaches 9 of the 9 states the dispatchers of the two committed ollvm-16 -fla functions can select, and reports a named reason for any state it does not reach rather than dropping it.
descriptors.external_oracle: both sides of this ratio are disrobe's. The denominator is read out of the sample's own compare tree rather than typed into the gate, and a second pass re-derives it by scanning every equality compare against the state register in a linear decode of the whole function, so a tree walk that stopped early is caught instead of shrinking its own denominator. That makes the count harder to fake, not externally graded: no other tool supplies the state list. Behavior is graded separately and more narrowly, by executing the flattened bytes and the re-emitted recovered bytes under the in-house x86 interpreter and comparing the return value against corpus/native/ollvm/probe_src.c, the committed C source the fixtures were built from.
descriptors.measured: 9 reached by the recovered program / 9 states the two committed dispatchers can select

descriptors.claim: disrobe's taint engine recalls 93 of 190 labeled command-injection flows in the NIST SARD Juliet Test Suite's char/system/.c CWE-78 slice at gcc 16.1.0 -O2, with 0 false positives across every populated category, and the ground truth is the corpus's own manifest.xml and Flow Variant header, never a value authored in this repository.
descriptors.external_oracle: the NIST SARD Juliet Test Suite for C/C++ v1.3 (2017-10-01), CWE-78 OS Command Injection, char/system/.c files only. Ground truth is manifest.xml's own flaw line plus each file's own Flow Variant header, parsed by a typed reader that rejects an unrecognized line rather than defaulting. A finding is a true positive only when it names a function on the corpus's own bad-labeled call chain, and a false positive when it names one on the good-labeled chain; every group contributes exactly one bad-side and one good-side verdict, so a case cannot be silently dropped.
descriptors.reproduce: cargo test -p disrobe-taint --test graded_corpus published_juliet_o2_bars_match_the_pinned_floors (unconditional, needs no corpus: compares xtask/data/recovery.json against the pinned floors below, and runs in CI); DISROBE_REQUIRE_JULIET_CORPUS=1 cargo test -p disrobe-taint --test graded_corpus juliet_cwe78_command_injection_precision_recall_o2 (re-derives the floor against the real corpus; local-only, since the corpus is fetched to a scratch cache by pinned URL and sha256, never committed, and CI does not provision it)
